nodes.bodyText:
Hello all,
While loading multiple adapters with peft, I get an _IncompatibleKeys object with many missing_keys, but no incompatible_keys. I have raised an issue on peft here: huggingface/peft#1323. However, the answer that I got was that:

The _IncompatibleKeys comes up because of this line in set_peft_model_state_dict :


load_result = model.load_state_dict(peft_model_state_dict, strict=False)
Here, peft_model_state_dict is the state dict containing our new adapter weights (and ONLY the new adapter weights). Internally, PEFT > will rename the state dict entries to use the new adapter name adapter2. So in my case, it looks like:


['base_model.model.transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.lora_A.adapter2.weight', 'base_model.model.transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.lora_B.adapter2.weight', ......]
When you call load_adapter, a new adapter is initialized first using add_adapter here. Next, when > we load the state dict for the new adapter using model.load_state_dict, PyTorch finds that all the entries for the new adapter are present, but the entries for the base model and the old adapter are not present. Hence you get a _IncompatibleKeys load result with a long list of missing keys (and no unexpected keys).

This means that the issue was cased by PyTorch not finding the keys for the base model and old adapter in the new state dict, which contains only entries for the new adapter's state dict. Therefore, it reports that there are missing keys. However, I note that the missing_keys attribute contains entries from both adapters. This means that the missing_keys are not simply the entries not in the new state dict.
Is this expected behavior? It appears that the parameters are actually loaded into the state dict, so is this warning superfluous?
cc @albanD @mruberry @jbschlosser @walterddr @mikaylagawarecki

🐛 Describe the bug
In the documentation, torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention has 7 parameters, 3 of which are positional.
However, when running the following code:
x = torch.randn(8, 16, 256)

# Works fine, returns Tensor of shape [8,16,256]
torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(x,x,x,attn_mask=None,dropout_p=0.0,is_causal=False,scale=None)
# Triggers a TypeError
torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(x,x,x,None,0.0,False,None)
The first call works fine, but the second call triggers this:
TypeError: scaled_dot_product_attention() takes from 3 to 6 positional arguments but 7 were given

Not naming the named arguments, even with the same values, results in this error. Am I missing a detail about Python?
This error happens on both the stable version 2.1 and on the latest nightly version 2.3.0 (result of collect_env). This happens on both macOS and Linux.

import torch
import torch.utils._pytree as pytree

class DoubleTensor(object):
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value

    @classmethod
    def __torch_function__(cls, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
        if kwargs is None:
            kwargs = {}
        new_args, new_kwargs = pytree.tree_map_only(DoubleTensor, lambda x: x.value, (args, kwargs))
        output = func(*new_args, **new_kwargs)
        return DoubleTensor(output * 2)

@torch.compile(backend="aot_eager", fullgraph=True)
def f(x):
    y = DoubleTensor(x)
    z = torch.mul(y, 1)

🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
For background discussion, please see:
https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/connecting-pytorch-sparse-tensors-with-mlir/195145
Given the following code:
import torch
import torch.export
import torch.sparse


class BikNet(torch.nn.Module):

  def __init__(self):
    super(BikNet, self).__init__()
    return

  def forward(self, x):
    return x.sum()


biknet = BikNet()
biknet.eval()

dense_input = torch.ones(64, 64)
sparse_input = dense_input.to_sparse_csr()

prog1 = torch.export.export(biknet, args=(dense_input,))
prog2 = torch.export.export(biknet, args=(sparse_input,))   # fails

Then prog1 yields the expected traced graph IR as follows:
ExportedProgram:
    class GraphModule(torch.nn.Module):
        def forward(self, l_x_: "f32[64, 64]"):
            # File: biknet.py:17, code: return x.sum()
            sum_1: "f32[]" = torch.ops.aten.sum.default(l_x_);  l_x_ = None
            return (sum_1,)

Graph signature: ExportGraphSignature(
  input_specs=[
    InputSpec(
    kind=<InputKind.USER_INPUT: 1>,
    arg=TensorArgument(name='l_x_'),
    target=None)
  ],
  output_specs=[
    OutputSpec(kind=<OutputKind.USER_OUTPUT: 1>,
    arg=TensorArgument(name='sum_1'),
    target=None)
    ])
Range constraints: {}

However, computing prog2 throws an exception when trying to compute the tensor's size (due to having no strides on CSR format when trying to multiply shapes and strides for size):
torch._dynamo.exc.InternalTorchDynamoError: Sparse CSR tensors do not have strides
A much more desired outcome would be to yield a similar traced graph as for the dense case, but where argument l_x is annotated with the torch.sparse_csr layout. That would enable compilers (in particular "sparse compilers") to build an IR where sparsity is reflected in the types (and not the code yet).
Alternatives
No response
Additional context
No response

🐛 Describe the bug
I have a setup where I am manually sharding weights for 2D parallelism and then constructing this as a DTensor using DTensor.from_local. Everything seems to work fine, except if I turn on sync_module_states=True, I get a nasty error:
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/torch/distributed/utils.py", line 307, in _sync_params_and_buffers
    dist._broadcast_coalesced(
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/torch/distributed/_tensor/api.py", line 280, in __torch_dispatch__
    return DTensor._op_dispatcher.dispatch(
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/torch/distributed/_tensor/dispatch.py", line 111, in dispatch
    op_info = self.unwrap_to_op_info(op_call, args, kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/torch/distributed/_tensor/dispatch.py", line 352, in unwrap_to_op_info
    assert mesh is not None, f"found no DeviceMesh from dtensor args for {op_call}!"
AssertionError: found no DeviceMesh from dtensor args for c10d.broadcast_.default!

I dug into the code, and it seems like at some point we have:
 c10d.broadcast_.default, args_list=([DTensor(local_tensor=tensor([ 0.0086,  0.0035,  0.0327,  ...,  0.0029, -0.0015, -0.0012],
       device='cuda:0'), device_mesh=DeviceMesh([0, 1], mesh_dim_names=('2d_parallel',)), placements=(Shard(dim=0),))], <torch.ScriptObject object at 0x181f7dc0>, 0, 0, True, -1)

         ARG isinstance(arg, dtensor.DTensor)=False, arg=[DTensor(local_tensor=tensor([ 0.0086,  0.0035,  0.0327,  ...,  0.0029, -0.0015, -0.0012],
       device='cuda:0'), device_mesh=DeviceMesh([0, 1], mesh_dim_names=('2d_parallel',)), placements=(Shard(dim=0),))]
         ARG isinstance(arg, dtensor.DTensor)=False, arg=<torch.ScriptObject object at 0x181f7dc0>
         ARG isinstance(arg, dtensor.DTensor)=False, arg=0
         ARG isinstance(arg, dtensor.DTensor)=False, arg=0
         ARG isinstance(arg, dtensor.DTensor)=False, arg=True
         ARG isinstance(arg, dtensor.DTensor)=False, arg=-1

so mesh is never set inside this function.
It seems DTensor does not support broadcast, which is needed to broadcast initial weights across all replicas with HSDP.

🐛 Describe the bug
Given a transformer language model compiled with:
model = torch.compile(model, mode="reduce-overhead", fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)
where the bulk of the task is computing next token logits for different prompts (MMLU), memory usage grows until reaching OOM.
Without torch.compile, there is no OOM.
I think this happens because different prompts are different lengths, so torch.compile records different paths for each different size, which eventually leads to an OOM.
It's a Llama2 model with a static kv-cache (the model from https://github.com/pytorch-labs/gpt-fast/blob/main/model.py). I call model.setup_caches(max_batch_size=1, max_seq_length=model.config.block_size) so the caches are not being adjusted ever.
Is there a way to set up the prompt to always be model.config.block_size tokens long, then mask out irrelevant tokens, so that there is only one path through model.forward? Or should I avoid torch.compile and setup batching to achieve a speedup?

Issue description
I am following the method of this blog Accelerating Generative AI with PyTorch: Segment Anything, Fast to accelerate LLaVA  inference.
When I experimented with the Semi-structured sparsity solution, I encountered a problem.
First, when I apply semi-structured sparse to the entire model, the memory explodes (cuda out of memory). But my A100 has 40960 MiB of video memory, which logically shouldn't be the case.
LLaVA is composed of Llama + CLIP, and the model structure is as follows.
LlavaLlamaForCausalLM(
   (model): LlavaLlamaModel(
     (embed_tokens): Embedding(32000, 5120, padding_idx=0)
     (layers): ModuleList(
       (0-39): 40 x LlamaDecoderLayer(
         (self_attn): LlamaAttention(

🐛 Describe the bug
If a DLPack is passed to torch from an external system whose data pointer is nullptr, torch never calls the deleter of that DLPack, leaking the DLPack metadata.
This is a legal and reasonable thing to do, e.g., for an array with no elements.
From inspecting the code, this looks like an instance of a common C++ bug where std::unique_ptr will not call its deleter if the underlying data pointer is nullptr, which it is in this case.

🐛 Describe the bug
Sharding and compiling a single Linear module works well, but trying to register an all-gather forward hook on it seems to break (edit: to be clear, I think the error is related to Dynamo trying to compile the collective for this device mesh, not the hook itself). Is this an unexpected way of using network.linear.register_forward_hook or a bug?
Here's a toy repro and the log:
import torch
from torch.distributed._tensor import DeviceMesh
from torch.distributed.tensor.parallel import parallelize_module, ColwiseParallel
from torch.distributed._tensor import Shard, distribute_tensor, Replicate
from torch.distributed import _functional_collectives as funcol

mesh = DeviceMesh("cuda", torch.arange(2))

class Test(torch.nn.Module):
  def __init__(self):
    super(Test, self).__init__()
    self.weight1 = torch.nn.Linear(in_features=128, out_features=128)
  def forward(self, input):
    return self.weight1(input)


class Network(torch.nn.Module):
  def __init__(self, mesh):
    super(Network, self).__init__()
    self.linear = Test()

    self.linear_parallelized = parallelize_module(self.linear, mesh, {"weight1": ColwiseParallel()})
    self.linear_compiled = torch.compile(self.linear_parallelized)

  def forward(self, input):
    out = self.linear_compiled(input)
    return out


network = Network(mesh)
network.linear.register_forward_hook(lambda _module, _input, output: funcol.all_gather_tensor(output, -1, mesh))

input = torch.rand([128, 128], requires_grad=True)
input = distribute_tensor(input, mesh, [Replicate()])
output = network(input)

x = torch.unsqueeze(output, -1)
labels = torch.unsqueeze(torch.randint(0, 128, (128,)), -1).cuda()

loss_func = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
loss = loss_func(x, labels)
loss.backward()

Log:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../dtensor_backward_funcol.py", line 40, in <module>
    output = network(input)

🐛 Describe the bug
the output of torch.nn.functional.kl_div in torch.compile mode differs from eager mode. Above is a .pkl file which includes a specific input leading to this issue. I tried to generate target randomly and don't encountered the error.
inputs.pkl.zip
to reproduce:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import os, pickle

class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
    def forward(self, input):  
        return torch.nn.functional.kl_div(input=input, reduction='none', target=inputs[0]['target'])        

x = torch.rand([1, 7, 3, 9, 9, 7], dtype=torch.float32)


model = Model().to(torch.device('cpu'))

🐛 Describe the bug
I have an IndexError on some machines observed in test_module_partitioner_functional_conv_relu_conv
It can be reproduced with this code:
import torch

class FunctionalConv2d(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.stride = (1, 1)
        self.padding = (0, 0)
        self.dilation = (1, 1)
        self.groups = 1

    def forward(self, x, weight, bias):
        return torch.nn.functional.conv2d(x, weight, bias, self.stride, self.padding, self.dilation, self.groups)

class M(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = FunctionalConv2d()
        self.conv2 = FunctionalConv2d()

    def forward(self, x, weight, bias):
        x = self.conv1(x, weight, bias)
        x = torch.nn.functional.relu(x)
        x = self.conv2(x, weight, bias)
        return x

inputs = (torch.randn(1, 3, 5, 5), torch.randn(3, 3, 3, 3), torch.rand(3))
gm, _ = torch._dynamo.export(M(), aten_graph=True)(*inputs)
The output is this:

Strangely the issue happens only on one system. I traced it and found that when it is working only "s0" is used as expr in the failing line while when it fails it also is x.
Checking the dim_constraints.solve method I found self._univariate_inequalities = {s0: {s0 <= 3, s0 >= 2}} where it works but {s0: {4*s0**3 - 4*s0**2 + s0 <= 2147483647, s0 >= 2, s0**3 <= 2147483647, s0 <= 2147483647}} on the failing system.
The solution in line 1856 of symbolic_shapes.py is then (2 <= s0) & (s0 <= 3) vs (2 <= s0) & (s0 <= CRootOf(4*x**3 - 4*x**2 + x - 2147483647, 0)) which explains where the x is coming from.
Using the logger in symbolic_shapes.py I observed a difference:
- [INFO] eval s0 <= 3 [guard added] at ome/s3248973/test_fx_failure.py:12 in forward (_subclasses/fake_tensor.py:677 in conv)

+ [INFO] eval 4*s0**3 - 4*s0**2 + s0 <= 2147483647 [guard added] (_subclasses/fake_tensor.py:677 in conv)

So it looks like for the broken system a real tensor instead of a FakeTensor is used leading to failure to deduce s0 <= 3 and instead introducing some s1 such that it later fails to solve the complex inequality.
I can't find a reason for this and am hoping for some insight from the devs. Maybe this issue is known already?

🐛 Describe the bug
I tried with pytorch from source and pip, and use then todo distributed DenseNet trainning job(I put my source code below). However, I found that pytorch from source finish trainning job slower than pytorch from pip. pytorch from pip can finish the distributed trainning job in about 420s, while pytorch from source will consume 735s. what's more, I also run the trainning job within single computer. pytorch from pip can finish the singletrainning job in about 170s(this feature is ok since I only use 1Gbps network transmission), while pytorch from source will consume 780s. It's quite strange because pytorch from pip do single trainning job faster than distributed job.
For distributed trainning job, I use two machines with the same environment, use gloo as backend and TCP as the transmission protocol.
and this is the DenseNet I use for trainning job. since the code is too long, I put it in a public gist and link it in this issue.
https://gist.github.com/sunbin21/80d2a88f6e8442fd3c067f8bf7bae7fc
When doing the distributed test, I use this command:
python syncBNforDenseNet.py -b gloo -ip 192.168.1.149 -p 23456 -r 0 -s 2
python syncBNforDenseNet.py -b gloo -ip 192.168.1.149 -p 23456 -r 1 -s 2
the first line is for machine 0 and the second line is for machine 1(192.168.1.149 is the ip address of machine 0). for single trainning job, I use this command
python syncBNforDenseNet.py -b gloo -ip 192.168.1.149 -p 23456 -r 0 -s 1

🐛 Describe the bug
When using torch.compile which input is a subclass of torch.Tensor, raise torch._dynamo.exc.InternalTorchDynamoError: ListIteratorVariable() has no type.
Below I create a really simple demo to reproduce the issue.
class MetaTensor(MetaObj, torch.Tensor):
    @staticmethod
    def __new__(cls, x, meta, *args, **kwargs):
        return super().__new__(cls, x, *args, **kwargs)
    
    def __init__(self, x, meta):
        self.meta = meta

    @staticmethod
    def update_meta(x):
        first_meta = x if isinstance(x, MetaObj) else 0

    @classmethod
    def __torch_function__(cls, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
        ret = super().__torch_function__(func, types, args, kwargs)
        fake_meta = MetaObj.generate_meta([ret])
        MetaTensor.update_meta(fake_meta)
        return ret

class MetaObj:
    @staticmethod
    def generate_meta(meta):
        for i in meta:
            yield i

def model(x):
    return x + 1

model_opt = torch.compile(model, mode="reduce-overhead")

input = MetaTensor(torch.randn(1, 3, 128, 128), meta={'a': 1})
out = model_opt(input)

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
In torch.compile mode and eager mode, torch.daig_embed should produce the same output for the same input. However, there seems to be some mistake leading to different values.
to reproduce:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
    def forward(self, input): 
        input = torch.diag_embed(input=input, dim1=-1,dim2=0,offset=1)        
        return input

x = torch.rand([8, 6, 8, 6, 6, 1], dtype=torch.float64)
model = Model().to(torch.device('cpu'))
eag = model(x)
opt = torch.compile(model.forward)(x)

same_val = torch.allclose(eag.to('cpu'), 
                            opt.to('cpu'), 
                            rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3, 
                            equal_nan=True)
if same_val == False : 
        raise ValueError('diff value')

🐛 Describe the bug
import torch

n, c, hi, wi = 1025, 2, 256, 256
ho, wo = 1024, 1024
input = torch.randn(n, c, hi, wi, dtype=torch.float32).cuda()
input.requires_grad_(True)
output_size = [ho, wo]
output = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(input, size=output_size, mode ='nearest')
grad_output = torch.randn(n, c, ho, wo, dtype=torch.float32).cuda()
output.backward(grad_output)
grad_input = input.grad
print(grad_input.cpu())
Why is there no error message when the size of grad_output in upsample::nearest2d backward() exceeds INT32_MAX, but only the wrong result is output? The values of grad_input are all 0 instead of correctly calculating the gradient.
From the source code, you can see that only TORCH_CHECK (grad_input.numel() <= std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max()) is performed  and grad_output is not checked, but the index of grad_output uses the int type.
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/UpSampleNearest2d.cu#L154

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/UpSampleNearest2d.cu#L412

Versions

pytorch 1.13 or 2.1

nodes.bodyText:
Context
I've been working on getting the Dynamo tests to reset the Dynamo state before and after each unittest, otherwise, the state from one test affects subsequent tests, leading to unexpected behavior.
However, Dynamo is not the only place where we have global state. We've ran into situations in the past where changing e.g. the global default dtype in one test had a downstream effect on other tests.
Can we make unittests better by better isolating them somehow?
Pitch
Some ideas:

One naive way to do this is to run each test in its own process, but this is probably not feasible due to the amount of overhead it adds to each test.
Another idea is to have some centralized place where "all pytorch state" is kept and reset this state before and after each test runs.
Linters for abuse of APIs that modify global state? For example, instead of using torch.set_default_dtype, we should use a context-manager version (if we have one) so it's clear the global state gets cleaned up. This would still require us to identify all of the APIs that do modify global state and put them somewhere.

cc @ZainRizvi @kit1980 @huydhn @clee2000 @janeyx99, @jbschlosser, @pytorch/pytorch-dev-infra for ideas
nodes.title: Better unittest isolation for global state

🐛 Describe the bug
The below test case uses DDPOptimizer with dynamic shapes. It splits the forward graph such that one of the split graphs has an input tensor with a symbolic expression in a dim. The split FX graph doesn't pass the symbolic shape variables in the arguments. For direct symbolic shapes, inductor is able to decipher the variable from the input tensor dims. However, for the case below, inductor fails when the dim is a symbolic expression.
Shouldn't FX graphs declare every variable, even if they represent symbolic shapes, explicitly as input argument or as an IR node output, before its use?
import os
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
from torch.nn import Linear
from torch.optim import SGD
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.multiprocessing as mp
from torch.nn.parallel import DistributedDataParallel as DDP
from torch._dynamo.backends.distributed import DDPOptimizer
import torch._dynamo as dynamo
from torch._inductor.compile_fx import compile_fx

os.environ["TORCH_COMPILE_DEBUG"] = "0"
dynamo.reset()

def setup(rank, world_size):
    os.environ['MASTER_ADDR'] = 'localhost'
    os.environ['MASTER_PORT'] = '12355'
    dist.init_process_group(backend="GLOO", rank=rank, world_size=world_size)

def cleanup():
    dist.destroy_process_group()

class ToyModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(ToyModel, self).__init__()
        self.lin1 = Linear(3 * 1024, 2 * 1024, bias=False)
        self.lin2 = Linear(2 * 1024, 2 * 1024, bias=False)
        self.lin3 = Linear(2 * 1024, 3 * 1024, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x):
        t1 = self.lin1(x).relu().add(1.0)
        t2 = self.lin2(t1).relu().pow(2.0)
        c1 = torch.cat((t1, t2))
        t3 = self.lin3(c1).relu().mul(2.0)
        return t3

def simple(rank, world_size, iterations):
    setup(rank, world_size)
    model = ToyModel()
    model = DDP(model, bucket_cap_mb=70)

    intensor = torch.rand(8 * 1024, 3 * 1024)

              bucket_bytes_cap=int(100 * 1024 * 1024),
              backend_compile_fn=compile_fx

🐛 Describe the bug
I want to synchronize the parameters by averaging them across all workers in distributed training.
In this specific setup, for some reason, doing that all_reduce on GPU (NCCL or Gloo) causes a CUDA OOM (see rwth-i6/returnn#1482, maybe #116177, maybe NVIDIA/nccl#962). So my workaround for this is to move the parameters to CPU first, then do the average (via Gloo), then move it back to GPU. The code is as follows:
for param in module.parameters():
    # Separately move each param to CPU (instead of the whole module), to safe CPU memory.
    param_cpu = param.to(torch.device("cpu"))
    # On CPU, we are likely using Gloo, and Gloo does not support AVG
    dist.all_reduce(param_cpu.data, op=dist.ReduceOp.SUM)
    param_cpu.data /= dist.get_world_size()
    param.data = param_cpu.to(param.device)
Is there anything wrong with this code?
This seem to cause a memory leak of CPU memory. I added some logs which print the used memory, and I see that exactly during this sync, the CPU memory always increases a bit. It's not much, so it trains for quite a while, but then at some point I get a CPU OOM.
More logs here: rwth-i6/returnn#1490

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
torch.compile(...) does not pass models containing RNN layers to custom compilers, see this example:
import torch

class Model1(torch.nn.Module):
        def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                self.rnn = torch.nn.RNN(3, 3, 3)

        def forward(self, x):
                return self.rnn(x)

class Model2(torch.nn.Module):
        def forward(self, x):
                return x*x

input = torch.rand(1, 2, 3)
model1 = Model1()
model2 = Model2()

def compiler(gm, example_inputs):
        print("## --- compiler called -- ##")
        print(gm)
        return gm

cmodel1 = torch.compile(model1, backend=compiler)
cmodel2 = torch.compile(model2, backend=compiler)

with torch.no_grad():
        print("# ---- Running Model1 ---- #")
        cmodel1(input)

        print("")
        print("# ---- Running Model2 ---- #")
        cmodel2(input)
Generates the following output.
# ---- Running Model1 ---- #

# ---- Running Model2 ---- #
## --- compiler called -- ##
GraphModule()



def forward(self, L_x_ : torch.Tensor):
    l_x_ = L_x_
    mul = l_x_ * l_x_;  l_x_ = None
    return (mul,)

# To see more debug info, please use `graph_module.print_readable()`

Output shows that the custom compiler does not get called with the RNN model, but works fine for the basic x*x model.

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
In Pytorch CPU build without MKL/BLAS the at::native::cpublas::gemm calls just gemm_stub which calls cpublas_gemm_impl which calls gemm_core_ which does not handle TransposeType::ConjTranspose at all, see https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/BlasKernel.cpp#L241.
Sample code:
import torch
t = torch.tensor([[1, 2+3j], [2+3j, 1j]])

print(t@t.conj_physical())
#tensor([[14.+0.j,  5.-5.j],
#        [ 5.+5.j, 14.+0.j]])

print(t@t.conj())
#tensor([[14.+0.j,  5.-5.j],
#        [ 5.+5.j, 14.+0.j]])

print(t@t.t().conj_physical())
#tensor([[14.+0.j,  5.-5.j],
#        [ 5.+5.j, 14.+0.j]])

print(t@t.t().conj())
#tensor([[-4.+12.j, -1.+5.j],
#        [-1.+5.j, -6.+12.j]])

but all 4 results should be the same because t is symmetric.
The problem also manifests by computing the covariance matrix (and correlation coefficient matrix -- that's how I found this, because of these failed tests in test/test_torch.py):
import numpy as np

print(torch.cov(t))
#tensor([[-3.+3.5000j,  1.-4.0000j],
#        [ 3.-3.5000j, -1.+4.0000j]])

print(np.cov(t.numpy()))
#[[ 5.+0.j -4.-2.j]
# [-4.+2.j  4.+0.j]]

because torch.cov performs the last multiplication in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/Correlation.cpp#L122.
Latest official Linux pip CPU pytorch 2.1.2 build is not affected because it is built with MKL.

I should note that I also see:
/home/dwood/yap/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/diffusers/image_processor.py:97: RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in cast
images = (images * 255).round().astype("uint8")
Do commits on a given date immediately make it into the nightly?  If there is a delay I suggest looking at:
commit 7fb09b804b8e5ce3209ba9f7707ec5f3c1c11681 (tag: ciflow/slow/7fb09b804b8e5ce3209ba9f7707ec5f3c1c11681)

    Re-land of https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/111011.
    
    The original PR ended up having a bad interaction with code that tried to run `torch.compile` under `with torch.inference_mode`, which caused some internal tests to fail.
...

Error logs
No response
Minified repro
import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline

pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
    'runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5',
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    variant="fp16",
    safety_checker=None,
    requires_safety_checker=False)
pipe.to("cuda")
pipe.unet = torch.compile(pipe.unet, mode='max-autotune')

prompt = 'cat riding a sheep on mars'

with torch.inference_mode():
    images = pipe(
        prompt, width=512, height=512,
        output_type="pil", return_dict=False)[0]
    images[0].save('img-bad.jpg')

if True:
    images = pipe(
        prompt, width=512, height=512,
        output_type="pil", return_dict=False)[0]
    images[0].save('img-good.jpg')
